title: SI base quantities and prefixes practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All contexts, wording, numbers and figure briefs are newly authored. The mapped P2 leaves inform SI base quantity and unit recall and classification. Prefix use is controlled by the syllabus outcome because the mapped P2 set contains no direct prefix-conversion leaf.

question_set_contract.difficulty_progression: prior-learning retrieval to base-pair recognition, prefix-symbol discrimination, single conversion, complete recall, multi-scale ordering and an integrated estimation-plus-conversion decision

questions.prompt: From the previous lesson, explain why writing 5.0000 kg is usually unsuitable for a rough estimate of a loaded school bag. State one physical check that would make the estimate more trustworthy.
Which row gives an SI base quantity with its correct SI base unit?
Which prefix symbol represents a multiplier of 10^6?
For each of the following SI base quantities, state the SI base-unit name and symbol: mass, length, time, electric current and temperature.
The diagram shows three recorded pulse durations. Convert 3.2 μs and 4.5 ms to seconds. Then place all three durations in order from shortest to longest.

figure.purpose: Assess conversion to a common scale before ordering measurements
figure.brief: Original Cambridge-inspired black-and-white line diagram of three separate digital timing cards labelled Pulse P: 3.2 μs, Pulse Q: 4.5 ms and Pulse R: 0.0060 s. Keep the cards equal in size and do not add arrows, converted values or ordering clues.
figure.alt_text: Three pulse timing cards show P as 3.2 microseconds, Q as 4.5 milliseconds and R as 0.0060 seconds.

questions.prompt: Three labels have fallen from length measurements made in a school laboratory. The diagram shows a classroom door beside the labels 2.05 km, 205 cm and 2.05 mm. Convert each value to metres. Use a reasonable physical estimate to identify the label that could describe the door height. Then state the SI base quantity being measured and its SI base-unit symbol.

figure.purpose: Combine prefix conversion with an earlier-module plausibility check in one spatially clear prompt
figure.brief: Original Cambridge-inspired black-and-white line drawing of a standard classroom door with a simple student silhouette beside it for scale. Place three loose unattached labels below: 2.05 km, 205 cm and 2.05 mm. Do not attach a label, add converted values or mark the correct choice.
figure.alt_text: A classroom door and student silhouette appear above three loose labels reading 2.05 kilometres, 205 centimetres and 2.05 millimetres.
